commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] Add per-case kernel profiles to vllm bench forward
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add `--profile-dir` to `vllm bench forward` (#61339): a per-kernel GPU time breakdown of each benchmarked batch, in a form an agent or a script can read and compare directly.

## Claims

- `--profile-dir DIR`: after timing, each case's graph is replayed 3 more times under `torch.profiler`. Every rank writes `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.trace.json.gz` (Perfetto) and `DIR/<case>.rank<r>.kernels.json` (GPU time per kernel per forward, sorted, with call counts and one full name per group). Rank 0's top kernels are printed and included in `--output-json`.
- Only the timed forward is counted: the in-graph KV restore and rank rendezvous that precede it in each replay are left out (reported as `pre_forward_us`), so the profile accounts for the same interval as `median_us`.
- `python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile A.kernels.json [B.kernels.json]` prints one summary, or a per-kernel diff of two (e.g. before/after a change) sorted by the largest change.
- Nsight Systems: each case's 3 profiled replays always run between `cudaProfilerStart`/`Stop` in an NVTX range `forward/<case>`, so `nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat --cuda-graph-trace=node` records just them, one small report per case (and per rank with `torchrun --no-python nsys ...`). `--profile-dir` and nsys can't share CUPTI; combining them fails with a clear message.
- Timing runs before profiling, so reported latencies are unchanged; without a profiler the extra 3 replays per case are the only cost.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 4 passed (GB200): new summary unit test; the end-to-end test now also runs --profile-dir
```

Llama-3.2-1B, 1 GPU: profiled forward span vs timed median: decode 1291 vs 1265 us, prefill 4755 vs 4498 us, prefix hit 1782 vs 1770 us (profiler overhead; prefill's own sample spread was 1.75%). Decode excluded 512 restore copies per replay (~830 us), as intended.

Nsight Systems (2025.5), Llama-3.2-1B: one ~680 KB report per case; `nsys stats --report nvtx_sum` shows the `forward/<case>` range and `cuda_gpu_kern_sum` matches the JSON summary (48 calls = 16 layers x 3 replays). DP2 via `torchrun --no-python nsys`: one report per rank per case. `--profile-dir` under nsys: fails with the CUPTI message.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (1 GB200 node), ~100K KV: all 4 ranks wrote traces and summaries; span vs median: decode b32 15731 vs 15734 us, b128 20087 vs 19975 us, prefill 16K 204.2 vs ~202 ms. Example (prefill 16K, rank 0):

```
        us      %  calls  kernel
   62146.8  30.35     40  deep_gemm::sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_impl
   22000.9  10.74    131  kernel_cutlass_kernel_flashinfergemmkernelsdense_blockscaled_gemm_sm100Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel
   20274.8   9.90     40  fmhaSm100fKernel_QkvE4m3OBfloat16H512PagedKvDenseDynamicTokenSparseP1VarSeqQ64Kv128PersistentKeepsAbForGen
   19139.9   9.35      2  _engram_lookup_kernel
   10378.6   5.07     23  vllm::topKPerRowPrefill
```

## Details

- Each replay's GPU activities are split into the `len(state_views)` restore copies (one copy each), the rendezvous all-reduce (multi-rank), and the forward. The summary checks that the activities divide evenly into replays and raises otherwise.
- Kernel names are grouped without return type, template and function arguments (`void ns::foo<T>(...)` -> `ns::foo`); generic launchers keep their first template argument (`cutlass::device_kernel<Op>`), CuTe DSL names drop their per-shape suffix. Non-kernel activities (memcpy/memset) keep their names.
- `span_us` is first-to-last forward activity and should track `median_us`; `busy_us` sums kernel durations and can exceed it with multi-stream overlap.
- Why both: `torch.profiler` needs no extra tooling, is scoped per case in-process, and is tested in CI, so it backs the agent-facing JSON summary and diff. Nsight Systems adds NVTX, NCCL, CPU-side and GPU-metric views that many users reach for; the capture range makes it record only the benchmarked replays instead of the whole process (load, JIT, warmup, timing).
- The model-microbenchmark skill gets a short "Kernel breakdown" section on both workflows (including keeping `--capture-range-end=repeat`, since nsys's default stops after the first case and leaves the bench hanging).
- Size: `profile.py` ~200 lines plus ~40 lines of wiring; tests and docs ~60.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds the `train-inference-consistency` agent skill under `.agents/skills/` (symlinked from `.claude/skills/`). It guides an agent through making RL training and vLLM rollout produce bitwise identical logprobs (true on-policy RL) while keeping rollout throughput close to the high-performance baseline.

## Claims

- A C0–C10 workflow with explicit pass criteria per gate, from module inventory and proxy model through inference batch / prefill-decode invariance, training forward and backward alignment, two-step RL acceptance, and delivery.
- Guides for the problems that come up on that path: mismatch localization and bisect, training forward and backward validation, which batch-invariant kernel each operator uses and what it costs, quantization conversion chain and QAT, rollout engine behavior (sampling seeds, prefix cache, MTP, R3), performance A/B, exact checkpoint resume, runtime provenance, and paired acceptance.
- The rules come from the DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning NVFP4 consistency work, where `actor/ppo_kl` and rollout/training logprob diff are 0 at every step.

## Validation

Docs only, no code change.

- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, including `check-agent-files` (frontmatter, symlink, SKILL.md line budget, every relative link and anchor resolves), `markdownlint-cli2` and `typos`.
- No model evaluation: the change does not affect vLLM behavior.

## Details

- Not a duplicate: no open PR adds a train-inference consistency skill (searched open PRs for "train-inference consistency skill", "batch invariant skill" and `.agents/skills`). `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` documents how to enable batch-invariant inference for users; the skill links to it and covers the training-side alignment and validation process that the docs do not.
- Layout follows `docs/contributing/editing-agent-instructions.md`: `SKILL.md` (31 lines) is the entry point and links to `workflow/`, `guides/` and `practices/`.
- The skill is large (16 files). Each guide is a single file with a symptom table and key rules at the top, so an agent loads only the guide for the problem at hand.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and translate this skill. The submitter has reviewed the content and is responsible for it.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][LoRA][MoE] Expert LoRA for FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4 experts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add expert LoRA to the fused FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE kernel for MXFP4 expert weights with BF16 activations (`TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts`, next to `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`). TP > 1 relies on #61235 (merged).

## Claims

- MXFP4 MoE models can serve expert LoRA adapters on `moe_backend="flashinfer_trtllm"` instead of falling back to Marlin / unfused Triton.
- Opt-in: `moe_backend="auto"` selects the same backend as before. `flashinfer_trtllm_afp8` (MXFP8 activations) with expert LoRA is rejected with an explicit reason.
- Requires FlashInfer >= 0.6.18 (`gemm1_lora_delta` on `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3987); vLLM pins 0.7.2.

## Validation

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly arm64 image built from `af7f9488c` (flashinfer-python 0.7.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130), NVIDIA GB300, with the changed files of this PR and #61235 backported onto that commit and mounted over the image. Not run on the PR base itself; the changed files apply to it without conflicts.

**Kernel-level** — `pytest tests/lora/test_trtllm_mxfp4_lora_moe.py -v`: 9 passed. Random MXFP4 weights through vLLM's TRTLLM weight conversion, float64 reference from the dequantized weights, with and without an FC1/FC2 bias:

- delta in `[up | gate]` order: output and FC1 activation within 2% relative error of the reference; the swapped order is off by more than 30%;
- zero delta vs. the non-LoRA path: within 2%;
- the four incoming delta layouts are converted exactly;
- oracle: unchanged without LoRA, `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` first with LoRA + BF16 activations, explicit error with MXFP8 activations.

**End-to-end** — `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, offline `LLM`, `enable_lora=True`, fixed-token logprobs (`prompt_logprobs`) of 16 prompts x 200 tokens. Adapters are seeded random expert-only LoRAs (rank 8, alpha 32, only `gate_up_proj` / `down_proj` nonzero; B std 0.01 = small, 0.05 = large). Reference: `moe_backend="triton_unfused"`, TP 1. On the reference the adapters move the logprobs by 0.53 (small) and 1.89 (large) mean abs. "Effect" is adapter minus base logprob per token; projection is `<new, ref> / <ref, ref>`.

| backend | TP | set | MAE vs ref | median abs | effect projection | effect correlation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 1 | base | 0.136 | 0.038 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.132 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.963 | 0.629 | 0.84 | 0.79 |
| `marlin` | 1 | base | 0.126 | 0.040 | - | - |
| | 1 | small | 0.137 | 0.046 | 0.81 | 0.86 |
| | 1 | large | 0.973 | 0.621 | 0.82 | 0.79 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 2 | base | 0.149 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.146 | 0.051 | 0.74 | 0.81 |
| | 2 | large | 1.023 | 0.665 | 0.81 | 0.76 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm`, without #61235 | 2 | small | 0.472 | 0.232 | 0.33 | 0.42 |
| | 2 | large | 1.703 | 1.193 | 0.54 | 0.49 |
| `triton_unfused` | 2 | base | 0.137 | 0.044 | - | - |
| | 2 | small | 0.144 | 0.051 | 0.80 | 0.84 |
| | 2 | large | 0.993 | 0.619 | 0.83 | 0.79 |

The base rows are the floor between two backends or TP sizes on this text (same size for Marlin and for Triton at TP 2 against Triton at TP 1; the mean is tail-heavy, see the median). With the small adapter the new backend stays on that floor; with either adapter it tracks the reference as closely as Marlin does. At TP 2 it needs #61235 (now on main). The large adapter breaks the model (mean logprob -4.6) and is only there to make the direction of the effect visible. Repeating a request gives identical logprobs on `flashinfer_trtllm` at TP 1 (Marlin: 0.07 MAE between two passes). One run per configuration.

**Throughput** — same model, TP 1, 64 concurrent requests, 256 output tokens each, output tokens/s (second of two passes):

| backend | base requests | with expert LoRA |
|---|---|---|
| `triton_unfused` | 5828 | 4593 |
| `marlin` | 10510 | 7047 |
| `flashinfer_trtllm` (this PR) | 13388 | 7699 |

Supplementary, on a 384-expert, top-6 MXFP4 MoE at TP 4 (prototype of this change on an older base, 128 requests of ~3.3k output tokens): with an expert adapter 1.5-1.65x the throughput of `triton_unfused` and 1.02-1.16x Marlin; base requests 2.5-2.7x `triton_unfused`.

Not validated: EP, `fully_sharded_loras`, per-expert (2D) adapters end-to-end, more than one loaded adapter, CUDA graph specialization per LoRA, GPT-OSS at TP 4 / 8. `ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` are clean on the changed files.

## Details

Design. `TrtLlmMxfp4LoRAExperts` subclasses `_TrtLlmLoRAExpertsBase` and reuses its flow unchanged: the gate/up delta is computed by punica and passed as `gemm1_lora_delta`, so the kernel adds it before the activation; the down delta is computed from the post-activation FC1 output the kernel returns, and the base finalize and the delta reduction happen in one FP32 pass. Kernel arguments (`gemm1_alpha/beta/clamp_limit`, unpadded hidden size) come from the existing `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsBase`.

Three things differ from the BF16 class, each behind the new `prepare_gemm1_lora_delta` hook or a small base change:

- FC1 bias. The kernel has one FC1 bias slot, used either by the static `gemm1_bias` or by the per-token delta. On the LoRA path the static bias (GPT-OSS has one) is un-shuffled to logical order and added to the delta; `gemm1_bias` is then not passed. The sum is rounded to BF16, the dtype the kernel takes for the delta.
- Delta layout. The kernel takes `[up | gate]` halves. Per-expert adapters already arrive that way (or as interleaved pairs for `SWIGLUOAI`); fused 3D adapters arrive in checkpoint row order. All four cases are converted.
- Hidden padding. MXFP4 TRTLLM pads the hidden size (2880 -> 3072 for GPT-OSS) and returns an unpadded output, so the shared finalize now writes `output.size(1)` columns instead of the padded width. No change for the BF16 class, where the two are equal. The modular kernel also sized its output from the padded input and asserted on the narrower result in the no-op finalize; it now asks the experts for the output hidden size (`FusedMoEExpertsModular.output_hidden_dim`, default: the input size; the TRTLLM MXFP4 experts return the unpadded size) and allocates `output` at that width up front, so the result is used without a copy on a single rank. This also applies to the non-LoRA `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular`. This was found by the end-to-end run, not by the kernel tests.

MXFP8 activations are not supported because the kernel then returns the FC1 activation as uint8 without block scales (observed with FlashInfer 0.6.18), so the down delta cannot be computed.

Limitations.

- DP is rejected (explicit `flashinfer_trtllm` + LoRA + DP raises, as before this PR): the inherited no-LoRA fast path reads the local batch's adapter flag, while under DP the experts see the gathered batch. `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts` has the same gap; left for a separate fix.
- Top-1 routing with the weight applied on the input double-weights through the shared LoRA base (also `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`); fixed separately in #62019.
- The kernel tests need SM100, so the H200/L4 LoRA CI shards skip them; they were run on GB300 only.
- Not chunked, like `TrtLlmBf16LoRAExperts`: the LoRA token mapping covers the whole batch. The TRTLLM-Gen grid limits one call to about `(65535 - num_experts) * 8 / top_k` tokens (~130k for GPT-OSS).
- `SITU` activation is not enabled for the LoRA class (untested).
- With a static FC1 bias, a delta far below the BF16 step of the bias is rounded away.

Related work, not duplicated: #47226 adds FlashInfer MoE LoRA for FP8 / MXFP8 / MxInt4 (not MXFP4, not updated since July) and uses the same opt-in rule; #34421 routes NVFP4 LoRA to Marlin; #61164 and #61165 fix other parts of the MoE LoRA path and do not overlap.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix Gemma 4 encoder CUDA graph capture OOM at startup
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #61045.

With `cudagraph_mm_encoder` on, Gemma 4 made every encoder CUDA graph capture buffer far bigger than any batch its token budget can hold. Because of this, `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` ran out of memory at engine start on a 32 GB GPU. This PR captures one graph per budget and per row width (70, 140 or 280 soft tokens). Each graph gets only as many rows as the budget can fill, so no capture buffer is larger than `budget * 9` patches.

Compared with #61092, this fix:

- Fixes the reported startup OOM. [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) limits the number of rows but keeps every row 2520 patches wide. On the reported setup, [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) still dies in encoder CUDA graph capture (`Tried to allocate 662.00 MiB ... 8.43 GiB allocated in private pools`), both with the issue's flags and with images only.
- Makes video graph output match eager output (mean cosine 0.9994). On [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) the graph rows stay 2520 patches wide but the replay gathers at 630, so video output stays wrong.
- Adds 4 CPU test cases. They fail on the old code and also on [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092). [61092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61092) adds no test.

## Claims

- With the issue's flags, `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` now starts on 1x RTX 5090 32 GB: 21 encoder graphs, 2.61 GiB CUDA graph pool. Before: OOM at startup (`Tried to allocate 6.69 GiB`).
- The images-only variant (`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}'`) also ran out of memory at startup before. It now starts and serves images.
- Encoder graph output now matches eager output for video and for batches of 70-token and 140-token images. On the old code these outputs were wrong.
- The change is only in `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py` (+49/-10). It uses the existing `capture_axes` support of the encoder CUDA graph manager. The manager and other models do not change.

## Validation

Setup: 1x NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB). vLLM commit `fe4df3df0eb703862c686b256e9fe44fa94c8945` (0.31.1rc1.dev296), with and without this patch.

Reproducer (the issue's command). No request is needed, because the failure happens at engine start:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --async-scheduling \
  --attention-config '{"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}' --moe-backend marlin \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 1}' \
  --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"num_frames": 32}}' \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'
```

Before: 4 runs out of 4 failed the same way. 3 ran in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-fe4df3df0eb703862c686b256e9fe44fa94c8945` image and 1 in an editable install of that commit.

```
EncoderCudaGraphManager initialized with paths={'default': [70, 140, 280, 560, 1120, 2240, 4096]}, max_batch_size=58, max_frames_per_batch=1856, use_dp=False, capture_axes=()
...
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py", line 1992, in encoder_cudagraph_forward
...
    pixel_values = 2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 6.69 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.45 GiB of which 4.94 GiB is free.
```

After: 3 runs out of 3 on the final code started:

```
EncoderCudaGraphManager initialized with paths={'default': [70, 140, 280, 560, 1120, 2240, 4096]}, max_batch_size=58, max_frames_per_batch=1856, use_dp=False, capture_axes=((70, 140, 280),)
Encoder CUDA graph capture complete. Captured 21 graphs across 1 paths.
CUDA graph pool memory: 2.61 GiB (actual), 2.99 GiB (estimated), difference: 0.39 GiB (14.8%).
Application startup complete.
```

The started servers answered every request. One run sent 14 concurrent 448x448 images, each showing a circle in one color, at temperature 0. Another run sent 1 image, 12 concurrent images and 4 videos of 32 frames. Each image answer named the circle's color.

Images only (same command with `{"image": 1, "video": 0}`, 1 run each):

- Old code: OOM in encoder graph capture, `Tried to allocate 644.00 MiB ... with 8.43 GiB allocated in private pools`.
- This PR: 21 graphs, 2.61 GiB graph pool, startup complete. 6 concurrent images were each answered with the right color.

Graph output against eager output. A script outside this PR called `cudagraph_manager.execute(...)` and `model.embed_multimodal(...)` on the same inputs. The table gives the mean cosine over the leading tokens that the prompt uses:

| Input | Old code | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 image, 280 tokens | 0.9994 | 0.9995 |
| Batch of 70-token or 140-token images | items after the first: near 0 | 0.9995 or better | | 1 video 480x336, 32 frames | 0.185 | 0.9994 |
| 2 videos 480x336, 16 frames each | 0.191 | 0.9994 |

The old code could not start with the issue's flags. For this comparison it ran with a smaller config: `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets=[2240]`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch=1`, `encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch=32`. The batch-of-images row came from separate runs with images only and 4 items per batch. These comparisons ran on an earlier revision of this patch. The later changes were a rename, test edits, and removing one capture row that no batch fills.

Unit tests (CPU, `device="meta"`):

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py
34 passed

# with the old gemma4_mm.py, -k "encoder_cudagraph or encoder_chunk"
E       assert 2520 == (70 * 9)
E       assert 1856 == 14
E       assert 630 == (280 * 9)
E       assert [280, 70] == [280, 280]
4 failed, 5 passed, 25 deselected
```

`pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: every hook passed or was skipped, including mypy and `check-test-tethering`.

## Details

Root cause: the Gemma 4 encoder graph takes pixels as `(rows, patches_per_row, 768)`, with one image or video frame per row. `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs` made this buffer too large in both dimensions:

1. Rows: it used `max(max_batch_size, max_frames_per_batch)` for every budget. With video on, that is `58 * 32 = 1856`. But every row is at least 70 soft tokens, so a batch that fits 4096 tokens has at most 58 rows.
2. Width: every row had the width of the widest image, `min(budget, 280) * 9 = 2520` patches. A video frame, or a 70-token image, needs only 630.

So the 4096-token graph got a `(1856, 2520, 768)` bf16 buffer of 7,184,056,320 bytes: the 6.69 GiB in the issue. The first operation of the patch embedder needs another tensor of the same size. Limiting only the rows is not enough. The 4096 graph then still runs the vision tower on about 4 times the patches its budget can hold and takes 8.57 GiB of graph pool, and the next budget's warm-up runs out of memory. The width problem alone also breaks image-only configs, where every budget of 280 or more gets 58 rows of 2520 patches.

The fix, all in `gemma4_mm.py`:

- `get_encoder_cudagraph_config` declares one capture axis: the row width in soft tokens, `(70, 140, 280)`, up to the configured maximum.
- `select_encoder_cudagraph_items` returns the batch's row width as the axis key: 70 for video frames, and the padded width for images.
- `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs` builds rows of exactly that width, and `min(max(max_batch_size, max_frames_per_batch), max(1, budget // width))` rows. The one-row minimum is there only so that capture works when one row is wider than the budget.
- The replay pads list images of mixed widths to the widest one. So `get_encoder_cudagraph_item_specs` sets `path_output_tokens` to that widest width, and the manager never packs more rows into a batch than its graph has. `output_tokens` stays the real count and is still used to slice the output. Note: the docstring of `EncoderItemSpec.path_output_tokens` says single-path models leave it empty. Gemma 4 now sets it on its one path, for this reason.

The graph row width now equals the replay gather width. That is why video and narrow-image graph output, which were wrong before, now match eager.

Trade-offs:

- With the issue's flags, encoder graphs go from 7 to 21, one per budget and width. 3 of them can never be replayed: budget 70 with widths 140 and 280, and budget 140 with width 280. Each is one row. Skipping them would need a change to the manager's capture loop.
- In a config that already worked (images only, budgets `[280, 1120, 2240]`, 4 items per batch), the graph pool grew from 0.93 to 1.12 GiB and the KV cache shrank from 7.71 to 7.46 GiB. This was measured before the final row-count change.
- A list of images of mixed widths is packed at its widest width. It can need a bigger budget, or run eagerly when no budget fits it. The output stays correct.

Not changed here. These are older defects that are the same before and after this PR, and each needs a different change:

- Video frames with padding (for example 320x240, 63 real tokens per frame): the graph path counts the padding slots, so its output is longer than eager output (2240 against 2016 tokens) and later frames are shifted.
- Images with `max_soft_tokens` 560 or 1120 crash when `cudagraph_mm_encoder` is on, because the vision config has no `num_soft_tokens` attribute.
- `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` fails at encoder graph capture.

## Purpose

Fixes a 3-5% decode regression in v0.32.0, caused by #56891.

#56891 changed automatic FlashInfer allreduce selection to use `trtllm` for every node-local process group. Before it, single-node runs used `mnnvl`, falling back to `trtllm` on nodes without NVSwitch multicast. The PR included no perf data, and on single-node NVSwitch systems `trtllm` is slower.

## Evidence

The perf-eval nightlies show a step in the 14 commits between the 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04 nightlies, and #56891 is the only distributed change among them. Only TP>1 workloads moved:

| workload | before (10-03) | after (10-04 on) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200 | ~5650 tok/s, TPOT 20.8 ms | ~5460 tok/s, TPOT 21.6 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP4, H200 (same host) | 10883 tok/s, TPOT 11.20 ms | 10571 tok/s, TPOT 11.54 ms |
| GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, B200 | ~2770 tok/s | ~2650-2720 tok/s |
| MiniMax-M3 TP8, H200 | TPOT 35.9 ms | TPOT 36.8 ms |
| gpt-oss-120b TP1, B200 | unchanged | unchanged |

A/B on the v0.32.0rc2 image with `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` forced:

| workload | default (`trtllm`) | `mnnvl` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4, 8xB200, 8k/1k conc 128 | 5462 tok/s, TPOT 21.78 ms | **5728 tok/s, TPOT 20.22 ms** |

For node-local groups, auto-selection goes back to `mnnvl` with `allow_trtllm_fallback=True`. The unit test's expectations are updated to match.

cc @elvircrn: is there a case where single-node `mnnvl` misbehaved that #56891 was fixing? The PR description only covers the multi-node cases.

commits.pr_title: [Model] DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL: stream language-model weights instead of sorting the checkpoint
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The DeepSeek-V4 VL wrapper and the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4.1 VL wrapper sort the whole mapped weight stream so that the `language_model.` group reaches the child loader contiguously. The NVIDIA children finalize fused expert weights inside `load_weights`, so the group must not be interleaved. `sorted()` materializes the iterator, so every tensor the loader yields is alive before the first copy:

- **Loaders that yield materialized tensors** (`--safetensors-load-strategy eager`, or `--load-format fastsafetensors`, which yields a separate tensor per weight): nearly the whole checkpoint is held at once (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is 475 GiB). #58782 reports host OOM from the same sort on the AMD V4.1 wrapper.
- **The default mmap views**: this costs no extra anonymous memory. But every shard stays mapped for the whole load and name order jumps between shards. In our runs that meant ~20–30 GiB more mapped page cache per rank, more storage reads and a slower load (below).

Contiguity needs only a non-interleaved group, not a total order. This PR adds `stream_language_model_first`, which yields `language_model.*` as it arrives and defers the rest (vision tower, aligner), cloned in case the loader reuses its buffers. Both wrappers use it.

**Not a duplicate:** #58782 applies the same idea to the AMD V4.1 wrapper as one part of a ROCm fix, and could reuse this helper. This PR covers the V4 wrapper and the NVIDIA V4.1 wrapper. #57733 keeps the in-load finalize, so the contiguity requirement stays.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py
```

The test is parametrized over both wrappers and uses the real `AutoWeightsLoader` with a language model that finalizes in `load_weights`. It asserts that a weight is loaded before the stream is drained, that the child is called once, and that it finalizes after all of its weights. It is registered in the Basic Models (Other) CUDA step.

## Test Result

Both cases pass on current main (GB10, torch 2.13.0+cu130). Without the change, both cases fail at the mid-stream assertion: the stream is drained before anything loads.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 on 4x DGX Spark with `--load-format auto`, page cache dropped before each boot. These runs used a 0.28.1-based build with the same change minus the clone. Two nodes had `read_ahead_kb=1024` and two had 128, the same in both arms, which is why reads vary by rank:

| | boots | read per rank | load, slowest rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| sorted | 1 | 179–357 GiB | 248 s |
| streamed | 2 | 158–265 GiB | 202 s, 212 s |

With `--load-format fastsafetensors`, #55985 and some fastsafetensors fixes that are not upstream yet, streaming is what lets this model load on a 121.7 GiB node at all: ~88 s, against 202–212 s for `auto` above.

This changes only the order in which weights reach the loader. The child's per-tensor loaders don't depend on order, and it still finalizes once, after all of its weights.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the change, the tests and the measurements. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and boots.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Host model recipes in recipes/
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Host the deployment recipes for models served by vLLM in this repository under `recipes/models/<hf_org>/<hf_repo>.yaml` (186 recipes). [recipes.vllm.ai](https://recipes.vllm.ai) keeps rendering them from [vllm-project/recipes](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes), which reads this directory at a pinned commit. Companion PR: vllm-project/recipes#1095.

## Claims

- **Recipes:** `recipes/models/` holds the 186 non-omni recipes, identical to vllm-project/recipes main (as of 92fb889) except that `meta.difficulty`, which nothing reads, is dropped. `recipes/models/` is excluded from the `typos` hook in `pyproject.toml`: the guides carry multilingual examples and model or flag names.
- **Rendering:** recipes.vllm.ai renders the same commands from this directory.
- **No engine changes:** nothing in the vLLM Python, C++ or Rust code or the package changes.
- **Ownership:** `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns `recipes/` to @esmeetu.
- **PR check:** `.github/workflows/recipes.yml` validates every PR that touches `recipes/`. It calls vllm-project/recipes' reusable `validate-recipes.yml`, which runs the same strict assemble and JSON API build the renderer runs after merge. It is read-only and needs no secrets, so it also runs for fork PRs.
- **Authoring docs:** the `model-recipes` agent skill now points recipe authoring at `recipes/models/`, and `recipes/README.md` explains how to preview a change.

## Validation

- **Rendering from this branch:** vllm-project/recipes#1095 pins `esmeetu/vllm@98ed489` (this branch). Its build produces 215 recipes, 186 of them from here and 29 omni recipes that stay in the recipes repo for now.
  - All 21,723 generated JSON files match the current recipes main, apart from a new `source` field in each file. The only other difference is the dropped `meta.difficulty`.
  - Preview: https://vllm-recipes-git-fork-esmeetu-content-sources-inferact-inc.vercel.app
- **pre-commit:** passes, including `typos`, `markdownlint`, `check-agent-files`, and the sign-off check.
- **CI:** no Buildkite test area depends on `recipes/`, so this PR triggers no GPU tests.

## Details

**Why here.** Recipe flags track vLLM's flags, kernels and defaults. Keeping the recipes next to the code lets a PR that renames or removes a flag update the affected recipes in the same change, and lets people with that context review them. Recently merged recipe changes show the coupling:
- vllm-project/recipes#1091 dropped the removed `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD`.
- vllm-project/recipes#1082 switched the ROCm attention backend after a regression in v0.31.0.

**Ownership after the split.**
| Content | Repository |
| --- | --- |
| Recipes for models served by vLLM | vllm (this PR) |
| Omni recipes | vllm-omni (follow-up) |
| Ascend NPU content | vllm-ascend, as overlays. An overlay can only add keys, and only for hardware its granted scope covers, so it can never change the NVIDIA/AMD commands. |
| Schema, hardware vocabulary, command synthesis, site, JSON API | vllm-project/recipes |

**How changes reach the site.** A workflow in vllm-project/recipes checks this directory every 20 minutes. When the directory's tree hash changes, it validates the new content with the full build and then commits the new pin, which redeploys the site. If validation fails, the site stays on the last good pin and an issue is opened.

**Merge order.** vllm-project/recipes#1097, which adds the reusable workflow this PR's `recipes` check calls, is merged, so the check now runs. After this PR merges, vllm-project/recipes#1095 switches the site to read these recipes from vLLM main and removes them from the recipes repo. From this PR's merge on, recipe edits go here.

**Open questions for maintainers.**
- Location: a top-level `recipes/` directory, or somewhere else?
- The PR check references the reusable workflow at `@main` rather than a pinned SHA, unlike vLLM's other workflows. That is deliberate: recipes are validated against the renderer that publishes them, so a pinned SHA would need a bump in vLLM for every schema change. Is that acceptable?
- Make the `Recipes` check required in branch protection? As written it runs only on PRs that touch `recipes/`, so a required check would wait forever on every other PR. Requiring it would mean dropping the `paths` filter and skipping the job internally.

**Limitations.**
- The change adds about 41k lines (1.7 MB) of YAML.
- Until both PRs merge, any recipe change merged to vllm-project/recipes main has to be re-synced here. One sync has been needed so far.
- Ascend content is still inline in these recipes. It moves to vllm-ascend overlays in a follow-up.
- vLLM PRs get no online preview yet. Preview locally from a vllm-project/recipes checkout, as `recipes/README.md` describes; a Vercel preview is a planned follow-up.
- Merged recipe changes reach recipes.vllm.ai within about 30 minutes, not immediately. vllm-project/recipes checks this directory every 20 minutes, validates the new content, and redeploys. If validation fails, the site keeps the previous version and an issue is opened.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep resumable sessions that stop while preempted
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58776.

With async scheduling, a resumable (streaming-input) request can be preempted while a step is still in flight. That step's output is delivered as stale output, and if it hits a stop condition the request stops in `PREEMPTED` state. Two things then go wrong:

1. **The session drops out of every queue.** `_handle_stopped_request` re-enqueues the resumable request, but the stopped-while-preempted cleanup in `update_from_output` removes it from `waiting`, `kv_holding_waiting` and `deferred_waiting`, including that new entry. The session is then in no queue and is never scheduled again. (Still the case after the queue rework in #58947 and the handoff fix in #58259.)
2. **The fold deletes the prompt.** `_update_request_as_session` keeps `all_token_ids[num_prompt_tokens:num_computed_tokens]` and deletes the rest. After preemption `num_computed_tokens == 0`, so it deletes the whole list, while `prompt_token_ids` (a separate list) is only extended; `num_prompt_tokens` then no longer matches `all_token_ids`, and the previous turn's output is lost.

Changes:

- After the stopped-while-preempted cleanup, re-enqueue requests that did not finish, so each ends up in exactly one queue.
- In the fold, keep up to `max(num_computed_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`. On a normal stop `num_computed_tokens == num_tokens - 1`, so nothing changes; after preemption the session keeps all but the final sampled token, and `num_computed_tokens` stays 0 so everything is recomputed.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for this path (`stopped_preempted_reqs`, streaming/resumable + preempt, `_update_request_as_session`, session hang symptoms); none found. #58668 fixes a different case where `num_computed_tokens` is wrong at the fold (a speculative step stopping on an accepted draft). Both PRs append a test to `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -k stop_while_preempted
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py -v
```

New tests in `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py`, using a real `AsyncScheduler`:

- `test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted` (next chunk queued before / after the stop) reproduces #58776. It asserts that the session is scheduled again, that `all_token_ids` and `prompt_token_ids` both hold the old prompt, the kept output and the new chunk, and that everything is recomputed.
- `test_non_resumable_request_stays_dequeued_after_stop_while_preempted` guards the re-enqueue: a request that finishes while preempted must stay out of the queues. It passes on main and fails if the `is_finished()` check is dropped.

## Test Result

`test_session_resumes_after_stop_while_preempted`, with each half of the fix:

| scheduler | result |
| --- | --- |
| main | both cases fail: tokens are `[20, 21]` (prompt and output lost) |
| re-enqueue fix only | both fail: same token loss |
| fold fix only | both fail: `KeyError`, the session is never scheduled |
| this PR | both pass |

- CPU, `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input`: 806 passed with this PR vs 804 on main. The only difference is the two cases above; the remaining 1 failure and 6 errors need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py`: 14 passed.
- GPU (GB200), `tests/v1/streaming_input` + the GPU-only core tests above: 19 passed, 2 errors. The errors are `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py`, which fails identically on main: engine profiling hits `assert prefill_query.shape[0] == num_prefill_tokens` in the FlashInfer backend with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` on this machine.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line.

## Impact (update)

Besides the client-visible hang, the parked variant leaks scheduler capacity. When the session stops while preempted with no continuation queued, it is parked as `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` is incremented — and the queue cleanup then drops the session from every queue. If no continuation ever arrives, the counter is never decremented: each occurrence permanently consumes one `max_num_active_reqs` admission slot (the `num_running = len(self.running) + self.num_waiting_for_streaming_input` accounting in `schedule()`), so repeated occurrences silently shrink admission capacity. Verified locally on main: after the preempted stop, the parked case leaves `num_waiting_for_streaming_input == 1` with the session in no queue; if a continuation later arrives the counter rebalances in `_update_request_as_session`, but the session itself is already lost.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER tuned configs to select a4w4 gemm kernel instead of env var

## Purpose

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM` is currently used to select the weight layout (preshuffled vs plain) for every layer. With preshuffled layout, ASM gemm is used for prefill and preshuffled Triton gemm for decode. 

In previous PRs, attempted to remove the environment variable altogether and default to on, but caused regressions because various models (Kimi, DS) do not have tuned preshuffled Triton decode kernels. Ideally we would like to have this active for the models that it helps (Llama, mostly) without the environment variable. 

This PR removes the environment variable and decides per layer at weight-load time. A layer takes the preshuffled (ASM) layout only when aiter has tuned configs for both the ASM and Triton preshuffled kernels. 

## Testing

### Unit tests

```
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py
```

commits.pr_title: [CI][Bugfix] Ignore AMD CI webhook no-op builds in /amd-ci run and retry
commits.pr_body:
Every push to a PR creates an amd-ci webhook build. bootstrap-amd.sh exits for those builds without running any tests ("AMD CI does not start automatically on PRs"), so they pass with nothing tested. The bot treated them as real runs:

1. /amd-ci run from a PR author without write access was refused with "AMD CI already ran on this commit" (for example, https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14851). Pushing again didn't help, because every push creates another no-op build.
2. /amd-ci retry picked the no-op build and replied "No failed jobs need retrying" instead of telling the author to use /amd-ci run.

The fix skips builds with source webhook for AMD CI commands in both places. This is the same condition bootstrap-amd.sh uses. Builds started from the Buildkite UI, or by comment, still count. /ci behavior is unchanged.

Test plan: new unit tests for both cases; they fail on main and pass with this change. All 62 tests in test_run_ci_command.py pass.


### Replay against real PR data

I replayed `run_ci_command.py` from upstream `main` and from this PR against the real data for #62032:
- the live PR from the GitHub API;
- every amd-ci build on the PR, from Buildkite. The only build on the head commit `f03aefad5b` is [#14851](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14851), a `webhook` build that ran no tests.

All writes (comments, reactions, branch updates, build create, retry) were stubbed and recorded, not sent. The `main` replay reproduces the bot's actual reply on #62032.

| Scenario (PR author without write access) | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/amd-ci run` (bot merges `main` into the stale branch, as in production) | ❌ "AMD CI already ran on this commit: …/builds/14851" | ✅ Merges `main`, then starts an AMD CI build on the new head |
| `/amd-ci run --allow-stale` | ❌ "AMD CI already ran on this commit: …/builds/14851" | ✅ Starts an AMD CI build on `f03aefad5b` |
| `/amd-ci retry` | Retries no-op #14851: "No failed, timed-out, or expired jobs need retrying" | "No AMD CI build exists for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` first." |
| `/amd-ci run` when a comment-triggered build already finished on the head | ❌ "already ran" | ❌ "already ran" (unchanged) |
| `/amd-ci run` when a Buildkite UI build already finished on the head | ❌ "already ran" | ❌ "already ran" (unchanged) |
| `/amd-ci retry` when a comment-triggered build failed on the head | Retries that build | Retries that build (unchanged) |

Unit tests: the two new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. All 62 tests in `test_run_ci_command.py` pass.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][OpenAI] Respect allowed_token_ids in beam search
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

OpenAI-compatible completion requests already accept `allowed_token_ids`, and the normal sampling path respects it. The beam-search path dropped that field while building `BeamSearchParams`, then ranked candidates from per-step logprobs that can include tokens outside the sampling mask, so a valid request could return HTTP 200 with forbidden `token_ids`.

This keeps `allowed_token_ids` on `BeamSearchParams`, forwards it from both completion and chat completion requests, and filters beam candidates before ranking. Small allowlists use `logprob_token_ids` so beam search can score the exact allowed set; the shared offline beam path also intersects request allowlists with structured-output grammar allowlists.

## Test Plan

I ran a real OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` reproduction on Qwen3-0.6B with `allowed_token_ids=[43096]`, where token 43096 decodes to `" banana"`. I ran the same server/client on current main, on this branch, and after reverting this branch diff, then ran ruff on the changed runtime files.

## Test Result

On main, the beam request returned forbidden token 12095 (`" Paris"`) while the normal sampling control returned allowed token 43096 (`" banana"`). On this branch, beam and sampling both returned token 43096; after reverting this branch diff, beam returned token 12095 again.

<details>
<summary>repro (serve command, client, main, branch, revert)</summary>

Environment:

```text

Base commit: 26eb87204d58d9d8a25c378fbaec9da23db3fb85
```

```bash
  --model /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --served-model-name qwen \
  --dtype bfloat16 \

  --enforce-eager \

  --port 18280 \

```

commits.pr_title: [Core][Spec Decode] Replace EAGLE group heuristics with explicit draft-layer tags
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`is_eagle_group` decides which KV cache groups take the EAGLE last-block drop. The planner used to guess these groups from `non_causal_multi_token_decode` and from "the group holding the last registered layer" (MTP, DeepSeek-V4), and only on some grouping paths. This PR replaces the guesses with an explicit per-layer tag that the runners report, so a group is flagged iff it holds a draft layer. Supersedes #41640 (closed; its compared per-model field changed grouping) and #56026 (adds another guessing rule).

## Claims

- DFlash / DSpark drafters on hybrid models no longer make every group take the drop, so Mamba groups keep their prefix-cache reuse (#57032, #54360).
- A drafter spanning several groups (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 DSpark) gets every one of its groups flagged, not only the group holding the last layer.
- Gemma4 MTP no longer flags an unrelated target group. Its drafter shares the target's KV, so no group holds draft-owned KV and the coordinator's existing "flag all" fallback applies.
- The flags survive pipeline parallelism. Before, the scheduler config (worker 0's projection) cleared the flag of every group with no layers on worker 0, so with PP >= 2 the draft groups on the last stage were never flagged and the coordinator flagged every group.
- New draft models need no planner code to be identified. Out-of-tree runners must tag draft specs to benefit; untagged runners keep the conservative "flag all" fallback.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU; the only failures need a GPU and fail the same way without this PR):

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py
```

`test_mtp.py` and `test_attn_utils.py` also pass in full on one GB200 (84 passed). `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` gives identical results with and without this PR (1843 passed, 10 skipped; the same 97 GPU-only failures on CPU).

`test_eagle_groups_are_the_groups_holding_draft_layers` checks, through `get_kv_cache_configs` and `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config`, that the scheduler flags exactly the groups holding draft layers for a uniform model, a Qwen3.5-like GDN hybrid with MTP, and an MLA + SWA-MLA drafter spanning two groups, with pp=1 and pp=2. Reverting the PP projection fix makes the pp=2 case fail.

End-to-end, Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B with `{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}`, prefix caching on, one GB200, main (`ae8f41238c`) vs this PR. The workload is 8 prompts sharing a ~2.2k-token prefix, sent in two waves, greedy, 128 output tokens:

| Metric | main | PR | PR repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefix hit rate, wave 1 / wave 2 | 0.4409 / 0.5039 | 0.4409 / 0.5039 | 0.4409 / 0.5039 |
| Mean acceptance length | 3.3065 | 3.3065 | 3.3065 |
| Wave-2 outputs equal wave-1 outputs | yes | yes | yes |
| GSM8K-250 flexible-extract | 0.760 | 0.764 | 0.752 |

The GSM8K delta (1/250) is below the PR repeat spread (3/250). Commands: `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, then `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 250 --gen_kwargs temperature=0.0`.

The DFlash-on-hybrid case could not be run end to end: the local Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B DFlash2 draft sets `sample_from_anchor: true`, which DFlash rejects at startup on main and on this PR alike.

## Details

- Speculators set `AttentionLayerBase.is_draft_layer` on their layers at load time (V2 already did; V1 now does too). Both runners copy it onto `KVCacheSpec.is_draft`.
- `KVCacheSpec.is_draft` describes ownership, not cache format, so it uses `compare=False`: it never changes equality, hashing, grouping, or the cross-worker spec check. The `merge` assertions skip `compare=False` fields, because a group can mix target and draft layers (Qwen3.5 MTP). The field is only meaningful on per-layer specs; groups expose `KVCacheGroupSpec.is_eagle_group`.
- `get_kv_cache_configs` sets `is_eagle_group` after `get_kv_cache_groups_from_builder`, so it also covers groupings from a model's `SupportsKVCacheGrouping` or a platform builder. Flags are only set when `use_eagle_block_drop()` is true.
- `_project_kv_cache_groups_to_worker` now keeps the global flag. Every `is_eagle_group` consumer (coordinator, OffloadingConnector scheduler, Mooncake store coordinator) runs on the scheduler side.
- Behavior change: on uniform models the OffloadingConnector now drops the tail chunk like the GPU coordinator. Newly flagged groups recompute one tail chunk on external hits; this is a performance cost, not a correctness one.
- HiSparse resident/hot specs are not tagged; their groups are not prefix-cacheable, so no hit lookup reads the flag.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] hadacore: don't load past the input on a partial last warp
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes an intermittent `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `hadacore::hadamard_transform_kernel`. Since Oct 15 it has crashed the `(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantization` step on main (nightly 95042, builds 95065 and 95066) and on PR runs (95016, 3 of 3 attempts). The crash happens in `test_per_token_kv_cache.py::test_reshape_and_cache_per_token_head[int4-0-16-128-1-42]` and aborts the whole pytest process.

**Cause:**
- The masked kernel variant (`enable_mask=true`) issues `cp.async` loads for all `num_chunks` chunks of a warp, even when the warp owns fewer (`real_num_chunks`).
- For the int4 per-token-head KV path, 42 tokens × 128 bf16 = 21 chunks of 256 elements, at 2 chunks per warp. So the last warp reads 512 bytes past the end of the input.
- That over-read only faults when the input ends at the end of a CUDA memory segment. Whether it does depends on what earlier tests left in the caching allocator. That's why it showed up when automatic sharding put `test_online.py` in the same process.
- The `cp.async.wait_group` counts further down already assume only `real_num_chunks` groups were committed (`switch(k + diff_num_chunks)`).

**Fix:** skip the loads past `real_num_chunks` in the masked variant.

## Test Plan

Repro on Buildkite, Quantization step only, on a throwaway branch:

| Build | What it ran | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [95264](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95264) | `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` alone, and after each single suspect file | passes |
| [95264](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95264) | after the full 8-file shard-4 order | **crash** |
| [95275](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95275) | full order, leaving one file out each time | crash unless `test_online.py` is left out |
| [95292](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95292) | **this fix**: full crashing order ×3, plus the file alone | **all pass** (244 passed / 25 skipped each run, 82 passed alone) |

## Overview

Preserve parser and generation failures in Cohere and Anthropic streaming responses. Follow the [review feedback](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61947#discussion_r4291298497) by exposing raw chat chunks from the shared generator and converting them at each API's output boundary.

## Claims

- Add `OpenAIServingChat.chat_completion_stream_generator_raw`, yielding `ChatCompletionStreamResponse | ErrorResponse` without SSE framing.
- Convert raw objects directly in Cohere and Anthropic, removing intermediate JSON serialization and reparsing. Both preserve the sanitized original error before or during output and close active blocks before the terminal error event.
- Preserve OpenAI's JSON fields, usage metadata and `[DONE]` termination, including when output serialization itself fails.

## Validation

| Targeted CPU tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Cohere protocol, routes and conversion | 213 passed |
| Anthropic request/response and stream conversion | 112 passed |
| OpenAI streaming, reasoning usage, logprobs and parallel tool parsing | 135 passed across two selections |
| Total | **460 passed** |

- The four new Anthropic error cases fail before the fix. Regression cases cover errors before the first chunk and during text, thinking and tool-use blocks.
- HTTP and official SDK checks pass for all three APIs across normal output, parser failure, early generation failure and failure after text output. Cohere/Anthropic checks also forbid intermediate `ChatCompletionStreamResponse` JSON serialization/parsing.
- A comparison against the published PR's original OpenAI generator matches JSON frames and final request metadata for 128 normal configurations and two error cases. Configurations vary usage, continuous usage, echo, token IDs, prompt text, fingerprint and `n=1/2`.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and test CI association, and `git diff --check` pass. Existing Buildkite entrypoint jobs cover all three test files.
- Validation uses controlled engine outputs without model weights or GPU execution. No model-generation, accuracy or performance evaluation was run.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_conversion.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_streaming.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/cohere -q

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/anthropic -q

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion \
  -k 'streaming_chunks_keep_usage_and_metadata or streaming_errors_preserve_envelope or streaming_serialization_failure_emits_error_and_done or chat_streaming_metrics_ride_on_usage_chunk or streaming_reasoning_usage_counts_across_deltas or streaming_reasoning_usage_lifecycle_edges or streaming_logprobs_kept_when_parser_suppresses_delta' -q

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion \
  -k streaming_n_gt1_independent_tool_parsers -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/cohere/serving.py \
  vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_streaming.py \
  tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py

git diff --check
```

</details>

## Details

The shared generator can produce either a normal chat chunk or an `ErrorResponse`. Both API adapters previously expected serialized normal chunks, so an error envelope caused a second validation failure. Cohere could discard it before the first normal chunk; Anthropic replaced the original cause with the validation error.

Extract the existing generation loop into `chat_completion_stream_generator_raw`. OpenAI's existing generator serializes these objects and appends `[DONE]`; Cohere and Anthropic override that serialization boundary to produce their own events directly. Request preprocessing, admission checks and KV-transfer rejection cleanup keep their existing entry points.

Cohere retains its `message-end(ERROR)` followed by `[DONE]`. Anthropic now closes an open block, emits an `error` event with the original sanitized message, and terminates without a success `message_stop`. Normal stream exhaustion still performs block flushing and protocol termination. In-stream failures remain HTTP 200 and are communicated through SSE.

This extends the existing PR as requested; no additional PR was opened. Related [#60309](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60309) handles HTTP error mapping and [#61825](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61825) handles Cohere REQUIRED/tools validation; neither fixes these streaming adapters.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in CuTe DSL kernel for MLA attention over cached context. Default dispatch and new-token prefill remain unchanged.

```bash
--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"trtllm_ragged_backend":"cute-dsl"}'
```

For Kimi K3, this requires FP8 KV cache.

## Claims

- Enable CuTe context prefill without changing the default TRTLLM path.
- Align packed indptrs on the CPU, avoiding additional GPU copies.
- Reject unsupported dimensions and dtypes before kernel launch.

This is separate from #56784, which adds CuTe decode selection.

## Validation

Validated on GB300 with FlashInfer 0.7.1: **76 passed, 49 skipped** across kernel correctness, chunk metadata, and prefill selector/registry tests.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  -k test_chunked_context_backend_correctness
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py
```

CUDA-graph microbenchmarks with Kimi's 12 local heads, FP8 Q/K/V, BF16 output, and packed V:

| Query tokens | Cached-context tokens | TRTLLM µs | CuTe µs | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,024 | 8,192 | 71.8 | 56.2 | 1.28× |
| 8,192 | 8,192 | 221.0 | 184.8 | 1.20× |
| 16,384 | 8,192 | 467.2 | 369.8 | 1.26× |

Times are medians of three CUDA-graph timing rounds. These measure context attention, not whole-model throughput.

### End-to-end GSM8K

Validated on 8 GB300 GPUs (two 4-GPU nodes)

Kimi K3 MXFP4 target weights, DSpark draft weights, FlashInfer Python/cubin 0.7.1 and JIT-cache 0.7.1+cu130, TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3, and PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132.

**`max-num-batched-tokens=256` forces chunked prefill for the GSM8K prompts.** A short trace of a cold 775-token GSM8K prompt before evaluation confirmed **72 CuTe context-attention kernel launches on rank 0** (`kernel_cutlass_kernel_cuteblackwellkernelattentionfmhafmhaBlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionForward…`). Profiling was stopped before the full evaluation.

| Task | Questions | Few-shot | Flexible-extract exact match | Strict-match exact match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 1,319 | 5 | **96.36%** (1,271/1,319) | **96.29%** (1,270/1,319) |

Server configuration (run on each node; `NODE_RANK` is 0 or 1, and rank 1 also passes `--headless`). `TARGET_MODEL` and `DRAFT_MODEL` point to the local target/draft checkpoints:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
export VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=8

vllm serve "$TARGET_MODEL" \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$MASTER_ADDR" --master-port 29547 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --load-format fastsafetensors --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 256 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 32 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --profiler-config "{\"profiler\":\"torch\",\"torch_profiler_dir\":\"$TRACE_DIR\",\"torch_profiler_with_stack\":false}" \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"TRTLLM_RAGGED","use_prefill_query_quantization":true,"trtllm_ragged_backend":"cute-dsl"}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$DRAFT_MODEL\",\"attention_backend\":\"TOKENSPEED_MLA\",\"method\":\"dspark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":4,\"draft_sample_method\":\"greedy\",\"rejection_sample_method\":\"block\"}"
```

No online weight quantization, EP/SP, Mooncake, Dynamo, or synthetic speculative acceptance was enabled. Decode uses TokenSpeed MLA; CuTe is selected only for cached-context prefill. A cached-prefix extension smoke test passed before evaluation.

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,max_length=8192,max_gen_toks=256,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=32' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0 \
  --seed 42 --log_samples --output_path "$OUTPUT_DIR/gsm8k"
```

## Details

- CuTe requires FP8 queries for head dimension 192 and does not support dimension 256. Runtime validation and test skips share one compatibility helper until FlashInfer exposes a public API.
- CuTe requires packed V. Generic MLA's strided V is copied only when CuTe is selected; already-contiguous V incurs no copy.
- That copy can erase or reverse the speedup on small workloads, so CuTe remains opt-in.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Detokenize echoed prompts after truncation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/completions` with `echo=true` and `truncate_prompt_tokens` echoes the full, untruncated prompt for token-ID prompts, although the engine only sees the truncated tokens. The renderer detokenizes the prompt before `apply_post_tokenization` truncates it; this PR detokenizes after truncation instead, restoring the behavior from before the renderer refactor.

## Claims

- For token-ID prompts, the echoed `text` is now the decode of the tokens that reach the engine, so it agrees with `usage.prompt_tokens`, `logprobs.tokens` and `logprobs.text_offset`.
- Fixed for both truncation sides, and for streaming and non-streaming responses (both read `RequestOutput.prompt`).
- No change for text prompts, chat `echo`, or `/detokenize`.

## Validation

Real server on `a9fe30e9f6` (Qwen3-0.6B, RTX 4090, `--enforce-eager`), before and after the fix. Request: token IDs of `"one two three four five six seven eight"` (8 tokens) with `echo=true, max_tokens=1, logprobs=0, truncate_prompt_tokens=4`. `usage.prompt_tokens` is 4 in every case.

| `truncation_side` | Echoed `text` before | Echoed `text` after | `text_offset` indexes `text` correctly (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| unset (tokenizer default, left) | `one two three four five six seven eight com` | ` five six seven eight com` | no (`text[0:5] == "one t"` for token `" five"`) → yes |
| `left` | `one two three four five six seven eight com` | ` five six seven eight com` | no → yes |
| `right` | `one two three four five six seven eight five` | `one two three four five` | yes, but `text` contains 4 prompt tokens the model never saw → yes |

Tests:

- New `tests/renderers/test_completions.py::TestRenderPrompt::test_detokenization_matches_truncated_tokens` covers the sync and async paths with left and right truncation. It fails on `main` (the echoed prompt contains all 10 tokens) and passes with the fix.
- `pytest tests/renderers`: 632 passed. The 3 failures in `test_hf.py` need gated Hugging Face repos (`meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-1B`, `fixie-ai/ultravox-v0_5-llama-3_2-1b`, `google/paligemma-3b-mix-224`) that my machine has no access to.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -k "echo or truncation or single_completion or prompt_logprobs or batch_completions"`: 9 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, including mypy.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8011 --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager
python repro.py http://127.0.0.1:8011
```

```python
import sys

import requests

BASE = sys.argv[1]
model = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1/models").json()["data"][0]["id"]
ids = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/tokenize",
    json={"model": model, "prompt": "one two three four five six seven eight",
          "add_special_tokens": False},
).json()["tokens"]

for side in (None, "left", "right"):
    body = {"model": model, "prompt": ids, "echo": True, "max_tokens": 1,
            "temperature": 0, "logprobs": 0, "truncate_prompt_tokens": 4}
    if side:
        body["truncation_side"] = side
    choice = requests.post(f"{BASE}/v1/completions", json=body).json()["choices"][0]
    lp = choice["logprobs"]
    spans = [choice["text"][o:o + len(t)] for o, t in zip(lp["text_offset"], lp["tokens"])]
    print(side, repr(choice["text"]), "offsets consistent:", spans == lp["tokens"])
```

</details>

## Details

Root cause: in `BaseRenderer._tokenize_singleton_prompt` and its async twin, `needs_detokenization` decoded `prompt_token_ids` before `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization` applied `truncate_prompt_tokens`, so `prompt` described the original token list while `prompt_token_ids` was truncated. `needs_detokenization` is only set for completions/chat `echo` (without `return_token_ids`) and `/detokenize`. Before the renderer refactor, `OpenAIServing._normalize_prompt_tokens_to_input` truncated first and decoded the truncated IDs (see `v0.10.1`).

Limitation: text prompts keep echoing the original string, as they did in `v0.10.1` (the Rust frontend also echoes the request prompt). Aligning that would need the renderer to know whether tokenizer-side truncation actually dropped tokens; I left it out to keep this fix small, and can follow up if maintainers want it.

Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR for this (searched "echo truncate", "detokenize prompt", "truncate_prompt_tokens", "truncation_side", "echo text_offset"). #61363 and #61524 change which special tokens truncation keeps, not when the echoed text is decoded.

AI assistance was used to find this bug, write the fix and the test, and run the validation shown above.

## Overview

Enable MoRIIO WRITE for hybrid attention and Mamba/KDA models, including DSpark. This extends the hybrid READ support in #51052 and #57700 using existing transfer plans and post-draft save finalization.

## Claims

- Transfer attention KV, convolution and SSM state with per-group identity and completion accounting.
- Resolve the live final prefill state, exclude speculative scratch slots and publish matching N-1 token accounting.
- Use native `wait_all` with a finite deadline and a bounded fallback for older MoRI versions; nonblocking progress is unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased onto `642c18d64c`. The complete MoRIIO suite passed **274 tests**, followed by **3** block-state and **12** adjacent scheduler tests (**289 passed**). Changed Python files pass Ruff check and formatting. Full pre-commit installation was blocked by a certificate error while fetching actionlint.

```bash
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_scheduler_kv_connector_override.py
uv run --no-project python -m pytest -q -o addopts='' tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'hybrid or mamba or remote_kv or async_load or pending_push'
```

Real-weight GSM8K uses all 1,319 questions, concurrency 64, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42 and at most 256 output tokens.

| Validation | Control | Hybrid WRITE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current revision: Kimi-K3, TP8/DCP8, DSpark K4, block verification | Direct decode: 1,244/1,319 (94.31%) | Two runs: 1,232/1,319 (93.40%) and 1,253/1,319 (95.00%) |
| Previous revision: Kimi-Linear, TP2/DCP2, no speculation | READ: 1,167/1,319 (88.48%) | 1,171/1,319 (88.78%) |

Current K3 runs use connector revision `70c6fbfff9` on runtime `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`, FP8 KV, FP32 recurrent state, A8W4, align-mode caching, GMU 0.90 and explicit P16/D40 GiB KV budgets per rank. The first full WRITE run imported 836,896 prompt tokens and recorded 67.86% real draft acceptance. Each full evaluation had one empty answer; the measurements show run-to-run variation, not bit-exact equivalence or a performance comparison. The previous Kimi-Linear evaluation used runtime `43b4aaea3`; it has not been repeated after this rebase.

```bash
uv run --no-project python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0 --seed 42 --max-tokens 256 --request-timeout-seconds 3600
```

The existing connector CI suite covers the unit tests. Distributed model evaluations were run separately.

Serving completed without engine termination or RDMA transfer failures. Prefill logged recoverable hipBLASLt fallback warnings; these runs are not a warning-free runtime qualification.

## Details

The three commits separate bounded completion waiting, grouped hybrid WRITE and DSpark support. Changes are confined to MoRIIO, its tests and its usage guide; no scheduler, model-runner, sampler or router implementation changes are needed.

1. Decode advertises allocated block IDs in transfer-group order.
2. Prefill resolves the live final slots and writes attention KV plus convolution and SSM state for the N-1 prompt.
3. Decode waits for all transfers before consuming the imported state and recomputing the final prompt token. A complete coupled local hit releases the producer without an empty remote load.

Set `read_mode: false` in both roles' `kv_connector_extra_config`, use matching cache layouts and TP sizes, and enable `--mamba-cache-mode align`. For DSpark, configure the same draft model on both roles. Sliding-window WRITE and other hybrid speculative methods remain unsupported. READ and plain-attention WRITE wire formats are preserved.

This adds hybrid recurrent-state WRITE, rather than duplicating attention registration work in #58585 or READ lifecycle work in #58968. The rebase retains upstream #57705 local-hit release and failure routing, per-layer registration geometry and one-shot receive guards.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm][Bugfix] DeepSeek V4.1: don't pass expert intermediate padding to AITER
commits.pr_body:
AITER 0.1.25's FlyDSL MoE (ROCm/aiter#6125 configs) leaves the padded intermediate columns unwritten when told about the padding, so stage 2 reads stale memory and small decode batches (M <= 4 tokens) can come out NaN. This hits DeepSeek V4.1 at TP4, where the per-rank expert intermediate size is padded 576 -> 640.

Pass intermediate_pad=0 for V4.1's routed experts so AITER computes over the zero padding instead of skipping it, which is exact. DeepSeek V4 never pads the expert intermediate size and is unchanged. Revert once vLLM pins an AITER with the fix https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6598.

This hotfix was developed to resolve the flakiness in the newly added test group `(MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics`

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Sampler] Speed up the small-batch split top-p pipeline
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The small-batch split top-p pipeline (#54651) caps its grid at one program per SM (`S * B <= num_SMs`), and at that occupancy its step kernels are latency-bound. On a 148-SM GPU S drops to 2 at 38 rows, so a top-p call at 38-64 rows (e.g. 8 requests x 8 spec-decode verify tokens) takes about twice as long as at 37 rows. This PR makes two changes:

1. It keeps splitting rows past one wave while each slice still spans at least 7168 vocab entries.
2. It lets MRV2 skip the split pipeline when no row is top-p-only. Today the pipeline is still launched in that case, as 7 kernels whose programs all exit immediately.

cc @njhill

## Claims

- With the `has_topp_only_rows` hint that MRV2 passes, `apply_top_k_top_p` on <= 64 rows is as fast or faster for every row mix measured: all top-p-only, half and half, and all top-k on both GPUs, plus 1, 10% and 25% top-p-only rows on B300. This holds on B300 (148 SMs) and H200 (132 SMs), across the vocab sizes of current models (120K-262K, plus 32K). Main -> this PR:
  - Top-p-only rows, where main is at S=2: 1.22-2.16x on B300 and 1.05-1.90x on H200.
  - Batches that mix top-k rows with top-p-only rows, B >= 32, V >= 120K: 1.43-2.70x. At 32K, where S changes only from B=38 on B300 and B=34 on H200, it is 1.00-1.62x. The fewer top-p-only rows, the bigger the win: with a single top-p-only row, up to 3.7x at V=151936 and 4.4x at V=262144 (B300).
  - Batches where every row has top-k (e.g. the Qwen3.8 and Gemma 4 defaults): 1.00-1.21x. MRV2 no longer launches the split pipeline for them.
  - The worst ratio, 0.97x, is in configs where nothing changes, within the A/A noise. Callers that do not pass the hint get the same gains, except that all-top-k batches run at 0.90-0.98x (see Change 2).
- Real MiMo-V2.6 spec-decode verify rows (top_p 0.95) on B300: 561 -> 219 us at B=38 (2.56x) and 565 -> 318 us at B=64 (1.78x).
- End to end on the Triton sampler path (B300):
  - Llama-3-8B-Instruct, seeded top-p, c=48: median ITL -5.1%.
  - MiMo-V2.6-Pro TP4 with DFlash K=7, c=8: top-p goes from 558 to 301 us per step, and GPU busy time excluding MoE GEMMs drops by 0.27 ms of a 22.7 ms decode step.

## Validation

**Tests**, on fa75d3456d + this PR:
- B300: `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/sample/test_sampling_params_e2e.py tests/model_executor/test_watermark_sample_warmup.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py`: 287 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm only).
- B300: `cd tests && pytest watermarking`, in its own session as CI runs it: 191 passed, 3 skipped. In a shared session, the default device that `test_topk_topp_sampler.py` sets leaks into these CPU tests; that is unrelated to this PR.
- H200: `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`: 140 passed, 1 skipped. This ran on the revision before the new test gained its monkeypatch; the kernel code is the same.
- New tests:
  - B=48 in `test_topp_only` and `test_topk_and_topp`. On 128-152-SM GPUs this is the only tested size where main uses S=2.
  - `test_skip_split_without_topp_only_rows`: with `has_topp_only_rows=False` the split pipeline is not launched, and the result is bitwise identical, including for a grammar-masked row.
  - `test_has_topp_only_rows`: covers MRV2 `SamplingStates`, including top_k values that disable top-k.
- CI runs `tests/v1/sample` on H200 MIG and MI355.

**Microbenchmark setup.** Calls are to `apply_top_k_top_p_triton`, one CUDA graph per variant, with variants interleaved and capture order alternated between configs. Each number is the median of 100 replays with L2 hot. On an earlier revision without the hint, cold L2 agreed within 0.07x.
- "main" is this tree with `_topp_split_count` patched back and no hint.
- "PR" passes `has_topp_only_rows` computed from k and p, as MRV2 does.
- A second capture of "PR" (A/A) gives the noise floor: 95% of configs fall within +-1.5%, the worst at 0.96x/1.05x.
- Logits are randn x 3; p=0.95 and k=50 unless stated. The script is below.

V=151936, main -> PR:

| rows | GPU | B=16 | B=32 | B=38 | B=48 | B=64 |

| top-p only | B300 | 1.09x | 1.01x | 1.93x | 1.52x | 1.29x |
| | H200 | 1.16x | 1.06x | 1.69x | 1.38x | 1.05x |
| half top-k, half top-p only | B300 | 1.09x | 1.50x | 2.44x | 2.16x | 1.86x |

S goes 8->16 at B=16 and 4->16 at B=32. It goes 2->16 from B=38 on B300 and from B=34 on H200; at B=34 the H200 speedups are 1.74x for top-p only and 2.13x for half top-k.

GB300 (152 SMs) shows the same picture at V=128K-262K: top-p only 1.18-1.94x where main is at S=2 (B >= 39), and mixed 1.43-2.55x at B >= 32. At 32K, where S changes, the numbers are 1.17-1.19x and 1.11-1.45x. These numbers come from an older vLLM tree with an earlier revision of this PR's `topk_topp_triton.py` swapped in. That revision used a 6144-entry floor, which picks the same S as 7168 at these vocab sizes, and predates the hint, so it covers only top-p-only and mixed rows.

**Serving on B300.** These runs used upstream 30e79c3a76, whose `topk_topp_triton.py` matches this PR's base, with the split-count change loaded in. Servers ran back to back on one node. Per-step times come from a 29-step torch-profiler window; ITL comes from the benchmark client.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, T=0.6, top_p=0.9, c=64, 6 runs per variant (2 servers x 3 seeds): main 73.25 +- 1.11, PR 73.82 +- 0.96.
